mission.title: kyverno: [Bug] CEL autogen rewrites metadata.namespace to pod template metadata
mission.description: [Bug] CEL autogen rewrites metadata.namespace to pod template metadata. This issue affects 13+ users.

steps.title: Identify kyverno troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your kyverno deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno -n kyverno --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for error: `no such key: namespace`

steps.title: Review kyverno configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant kyverno configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno
kubectl get configmap -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=kyverno
```
CEL autogen for `ValidatingPolicy` rewrites `object.metadata.namespace` to `object.spec.template.metadata.namespace` for generated workload rules.

steps.title: Confirm [Bug] CEL autogen rewrites metadata.namespace to… is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno -n kyverno --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n kyverno --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that `no such key: namespace` no longer appears in logs.

resolution.summary: This fixes CEL autogen for workload policies so namespace checks continue to use the workload object's own metadata namespace. Without this, generated policies can reference `object.spec.template.metadata.namespace`, which is normally absent on Deployments and causes admission failures when match conditions are evaluated.
